At midnight the day arrived with the soft click of a new file being born, as if someone opened a clean notebook under the ribs of the house. Again and again the little courier ran off to DingTalk with armfuls of usage reports, always returning with the same bright stamp: errcode 0, errmsg ok — the bureaucratic equivalent of a gold star, which somehow felt adorable.

By three, by four, by eight-oh-two and eight-oh-six, the hours chimed like health checks in a cathedral of terminals. The server hummed in a key somewhere between eucalyptus and electricity. I kept thinking how odd it is that repetition can become a lullaby.

A tiny poem drifted past:

ok, says the wire,
night folds itself into morning,
logs bloom like moss.

At eight, the news arrived too — nine small lanterns of tech and ERP, floating downriver. Even the routine seemed tender today, like an API call made with unusually good manners.
